title: sparse-output-inconsistency-customer-checklist-2026-08-22
content:
Purpose and audience:
- Quick internal draft to shape a short customer-facing status & post-incident checklist for cases where customers observe sparse or inconsistent outputs (missing labels, truncated structured fields, empty embeddings, or partially-formed JSON in streaming).
- Audience: Customer Success (CS), Solutions Eng (SE), Support L2, and the on-call service owner.

Context (notes to self):
- Recent incident: some tenants saw intermittent partial responses from hosted/chat/structured-output endpoints during a scaled autoscaling event on 2026-08-22. Root cause: combined KV-cache eviction + batching window misalignment that surfaced on longer-context prompts and structured-output mode.
- This doc bundles: 1) short status-page/blurb options, 2) customer validation checklist (what we ask them to run), 3) replay/consent flow language, 4) suggested postmortem summary for customers once RCA is done.

Status page snippet (short):
- Title: "Partial/Incomplete Responses for a subset of requests — Under investigation"
- Body (concise): "We are investigating reports of partial or inconsistent outputs from text and structured-output endpoints affecting a small subset of requests. Symptoms include truncated JSON fields, missing list elements, and empty embeddings. We have implemented mitigations and continue to monitor; customers can follow the checks below to verify impact and request replay support. Estimated initial impact window: 2026-08-22 03:10–03:47 UTC. Updates to follow as RCA completes."

Longer status page (if needed):
- What happened (plain): "At ~03:10 UTC a combination of rapid client request ramp and an autoscaling transition triggered an edge-case in KV cache eviction. Some active requests lost the prefix state used for structured generation; as a result a subset of responses were incomplete. We limited exposure by disabling a new batching heuristic and rolling back the KV cache TTL setting at 03:27 UTC; a full mitigation was in place by 03:47 UTC."
- What we're doing: "Monitoring, additional regression tests, rolling back new batching heuristic config, validating model-level KV cache behavior, and adding tenant-level rehydration diagnostics. We'll publish a technical RCA and a timeline within 3 business days."

Customer validation checklist (what to ask customers to run):
- 1) Canonical quick check (safe and non-invasive): Re-run the same request with identical inputs and request-id if available. If you observe the same incomplete output, capture the example and timestamp.
- 2) Logging sample: Provide the raw request body (prompt + metadata), the API key/tenant id, and the resulting response. If streaming, include the streaming session id.
- 3) SDK/Network: Confirm whether requests were retried by the client (ex: network-level 5xx retries) and whether any intermediate proxy/logging shows truncated responses.
- 4) Model & Route: Note the model name and route used (e.g., gpt-ree-7b/structured-output-route). If you have explicit model pins, include that; otherwise include the response headers we return (x-rw-model, x-rw-instance).
- 5) Timing: Provide local timestamps and approximate wall time for the request. Prefer UTC.

Minimal evidence package (what CS should ask for)
- oblig: request body (redact PII), response body, response headers, SDK trace if possible, tenant id, and a short one-line impact statement (user-facing effect).
- Optional but helpful: network trace (HAR or tcpdump snippet), streaming session logs, application logs showing how the incomplete output impacted downstream parsing.

Replay / remediation choices we will offer to customers (consent-driven)
- Option A — "No action" (customer accepts and we close): useful for low impact customers.
- Option B — "Selective replay": We can re-run the captured inputs through the same model variant in a safe isolated replay lane using frozen model weights and snapshot of recent config. This can help verify whether the output is deterministic and produce replacement outputs. NOTE: replays may not perfectly match original runtime conditions (timing, batching, KV state) — we disclose differences.
- Option C — "Full forensic replay": For enterprise customers with legal/regulatory needs, we can attempt a tenant-level replay while preserving stronger invariants (model pin, cached prefixes rehydrated where possible). This takes longer and requires explicit data access consent.

Suggested language for customer consent form (short):
"We can attempt to re-run (replay) your affected requests to verify outputs and, when possible, produce replacement responses. Replays will be run in a controlled environment and may not exactly match the original run due to runtime differences. Examples/data provided will be used solely for debugging and remediation and retained per your account data retention settings. Reply with 'CONSENT-REPLAY' and specify Option B or Option C to proceed. For compliance requests, include PO or ticket reference."

Internal routing & SLA for this checklist
- CS triage (within 30 minutes): gather minimal evidence package and tag issue with JIRA-INC-11234.
- SE engagement (within 2 hours) for customers requesting replay.
- Engineering RCA owner: infrastructure-oncall@redwood (SRE team) — expected update in 72 hours for technical RCA, 3 business days for full customer postmortem.

Customer-facing postmortem template (to be published when RCA complete)
- Title: "Post-incident summary — partial/fragmented outputs affecting some requests (2026-08-22)"
- TL;DR (1–2 lines): "A brief config+cache interaction produced partial outputs for a fraction of requests between 03:10–03:47 UTC; mitigations rolled out and subject tenants were monitored. No data loss was detected; some customers may choose replay for verification."
- Impact: "Scope (# tenants, % of requests, or targeted customers). If possible, include affected routes/models and examples (redacted)."
- Root cause: "Short summary that avoids deep internal jargon, e.g., 'a KV cache eviction path combined with a new batching heuristic led to loss of prefix state for some requests.'"
- Timeline: short chronological bullets with times and actions.
- Corrective actions: immediate, short-term, and long-term. e.g., rollback heuristic (done), additional validation tests (in flight), improved observability (next sprint), tenant-level KV rehydration tool (design initiated).
- Customer choices: replay options, verification steps, and contact points.

FAQ (customer-facing):
- Q: Will replay change my data?
  A: Replays are read-only; they are executed on a controlled isolated lane. We will not persist additional customer data beyond debug retention settings.
- Q: Will the replacement outputs be identical?
  A: Not guaranteed; differences can arise from timing, batching, and ephemeral cache state. Replays are to help verify content and restore functionality where feasible.
- Q: Was customer data exfiltrated?
  A: No evidence of exfiltration. Access logs and audit trails show no unauthorized data exports.

Open questions / decisions to make (internal):
- Do we want a short TTL for cached prefixes per tenant to reduce blast radius (config flag)?
- Should we allow customers to opt into automatic background replays for low-risk outputs? (privacy/ops cost tradeoff)
- For enterprise customers requesting full replay, what is the exact legal/PO documentation we need to collect?

Next steps (action items):
- [CS] Send initial status page blurb with link to this doc (ASAP).
- [SE] Prepare replay lane checklist and cost estimate for enterprise replays.
- [Eng SRE] Add deterministic test case for batched structured-output with long prefixes (this sprint).
- [Product] Decide on tenant opt-in background replay policy (next PM sync).

Useful snippets for quick paste into a status update email to customers:
- Short: "We are aware of / investigating reports of partial/incomplete responses affecting a small subset of requests. Mitigations are in place and we are offering replay verification for impacted requests. Please respond with request examples and 'CONSENT-REPLAY' if you would like us to attempt a replay."
- Technical short: "Affected: structured-output & streaming routes under a specific batching heuristic. Mitigated: rollback of the heuristic and KV TTL reset at 03:27 UTC; full monitoring resumed 03:47 UTC."

Notes (workflow):
- Keep customer-facing language simple; avoid overpromising identical replacements.
- Track all consent replies in JIRA and attach evidence packages.
- Preserve timestamps and headers for debugging.

-- end of draft --

Editor notes: add a sanitized example request/response pair once legal signs off on redaction template.
